newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina to consult banks on credit facility.
newsitem.headline: Argentina to consult banks on credit facility.

text.p: Argentina's undersecretary of finance Miguel Kiguel confirmed Friday Argentina plans to consult foreign investment banks about obtaining a credit facility to call on in case of financial crisis.
Setting up such a facility has been suggested by economists but this is the first time an official has confirmed the governemnt is examining it.
Kiguel also told reporters one of the reasons Argentina is issuing so much debt in the first quarter of the year is because "there are worries overseas about Argentina's ability to obtain financing."
Separately, Kiguel said the country intends to issue a $500 million treasury bond, or Bonte, in February. Argentina launched its first Bonte in December - a two-year isssue of $500 million.
He added that the stock of outstanding Treasury bills, or Letes, in the market will be raised to $3.0 billion this year from the current level of $2.0 billion.

"Investors think Argentina has to pass a test because it has to seek more money in international markets than in previous years," Kiguel said, referring to the large amount of issuance in the first quarter.
The government announced Tuesday it will issue a $2.0 billion global bond, split between a five- and a 20-year issue. A further $1.0 billion will be issued before April.

When the country completes the placement of those bonds, in addition to $2.0 billion worth of bonds placed in December to cover 1997 spending needs, only $3.5 billion will remain to be placed in international markets through the rest of 1997.

Kiguel also said it is possible Argentina will not issue another Bocon bond to cover pension payments in arrears following a court decision in a case brought by 70,000 pensioners. The government may opt to pay the pensioners directly from the 1998 budget.
The official repeated Argentina's new financing strategy is to place less but larger bond issues.

Apart from that, Kiguel said the roadshow the government has scheduled for the $2.0 billion global bond issue will make a greater effort to find more investors in different places. Apart from the usual financial centers, visits will also be made to cities like Milwaukee and Minneapolis.
Kiguel said Mexico had widened the scope of its roadshow ahead of a bond issued this week with great success.
